https://24.kg/en/article/president-sadyr.body: President of Kyrgyzstan Sadyr Japarov expressed dissatisfaction with the work of officials in Jalal-Abad region and law enforcement agencies, saying they had failed for years to resolve citizens’ problems. During a meeting with residents of Bazar-Korgon district, he demanded action on land and property disputes and an end to delays in handling public complaints. The president’s remarks followed numerous complaints from local residents. One woman said several families had been unable to resolve a land dispute for 10 years. According to her, eight families had purchased plots, obtained state-issued title documents and built houses, but another person later claimed ownership of the land. Following court proceedings, the families faced the threat of having their homes demolished. Japarov demanded an explanation as to why the dispute had remained unresolved for so long. After hearing from government representatives, he recalled that he had convened regional officials earlier this year and instructed them to identify similar conflicts and ensure they were resolved. «I gathered you at the beginning of the year, in March or April, and instructed you to identify such problems in every district, resolve them and bring them to a close. Do not force people to argue endlessly among themselves. It appears you have done nothing at all. The problems that existed at the beginning of the year remain unresolved, ” Sadyr Japarov said. He instructed regional officials, the prosecutor’s office, police and other relevant agencies to compile information on all complaints and work together to address them. «If you do not resolve these problems, who will? The governor, the regional prosecutor, the court, the State Committee for National Security, the Interior Ministry — everyone must look into them, ” the president stressed. He ordered the responsible officials to meet in early November, after his tour of the region, to review the accumulated complaints and address them individually. Japarov also criticized the practice of allowing complaints to remain under consideration for years without concrete results. During the meeting, another resident raised concerns over pension contributions by former employees of an enterprise. She said her appeals had repeatedly been redirected from one government agency to another, but the issue remained unresolved. After hearing explanations from prosecutors, Japarov demanded that the review be expedited. «Do not drag these matters out for years. If you can resolve them, do so. If you cannot, explain to the person what the law says and why the issue cannot be resolved, ” he said. The president emphasized that citizens must receive clear answers to their complaints rather than spend years going from one government office to another in search of a solution. He also ordered a renewed review of the circumstances surrounding the allocation of land plots outside officially transformed areas, including the actions of former local officials and cadastre employees.

The sides noted ongoing construction work on the foundation of the first reactor building, as well as progress in designing the nuclear power plant. Particular attention was given to training qualified personnel for Uzbekistan’s emerging nuclear industry. The sides examined opportunities to prepare specialists through the Tashkent branch of the National Research Nuclear University MEPhI and at Rosatom facilities. Mirziyoyev and Likhachev also considered plans to develop a dedicated residential town near the future nuclear power plant. The proposed settlement would feature energy-efficient housing, modern educational and healthcare facilities, sports centers and other social infrastructure designed to provide comfortable living conditions for workers and their families. Rosatom, established in 2007, is Russia’s state nuclear corporation, with operations spanning the nuclear fuel cycle, uranium mining and enrichment, nuclear fuel production, reactor design and construction, electricity generation, and radioactive waste management. The corporation also develops nuclear technologies and provides engineering services for international nuclear power projects. According to its corporate reporting, Rosatom encompasses more than 400 organizations and maintains an extensive international project portfolio. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Pere Joan Pons Sampietro, president of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) Parliamentary Assembly, in Tashkent on October 22 to explore ways to expand cooperation, including through stronger interparliamentary dialogue. This was announced in a statement published by the press service of the Uzbek President. The sides noted positive momentum in their engagement. Uzbekistan maintains a permanent delegation to the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly, whose members regularly participate in election observation missions in the country. In addition, cooperation has developed in environmental protection, migration and transport. A representative of Uzbekistan serves on the Parliamentary Assembly’s Special Committee on Migration. Mirziyoyev and Pons Sampietro also exchanged views on international issues, including ways to deepen regional cooperation across Central Asia. To expand practical cooperation, the sides agreed to develop a joint roadmap outlining new priority areas for engagement, according to the statement. The agreement is expected to provide a framework for advancing cooperation between Uzbekistan and the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly, particularly in parliamentary dialogue and the areas identified as priorities during the meeting. The OSCE is the world’s largest regional security organization, bringing together 57 participating states across Europe, Central Asia and North America. Established in its current form in 1995, the organization promotes stability, peace and democracy through political dialogue and practical cooperation. Its work covers three main areas: politico-military security, economic and environmental cooperation, and human rights and democratic governance. These priorities include conflict prevention, election observation, migration, environmental protection and strengthening democratic institutions. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4238187..body: Home Azerbaijan Azerbaijan’s parliament receives draft state budget for 2027 Azerbaijan News 23 October 2026 10:12 (UTC +04:00) Photo: wikipedia Alish Abdulla Parliamentary Correspondent Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 23. Azerbaijan's state budget revenues for 2027 are projected at 39.25 billion manat ($23.09 billion), while expenditures are projected at 42.4 billion manat ($24.94 billion). This was reported in the draft law on the 2027 state budget submitted to the Azerbaijani parliament. The main sources of budget revenue include taxes, customs duties, receipts from state property, dividends from state enterprises, and transfers to the state budget. The largest shares of state budget revenue for 2027 are expected to come from value-added tax (VAT), at nearly 9.39 billion manat ($5.52 billion); corporate income tax, at 6.98 billion manat ($4.11 billion); and personal income tax, at 3.07 billion manat ($1.81 billion). The upper limit of the transfer to the state budget from the relevant institution is set at 11.9 billion manat ($7 billion). The main areas of budget spending include economic activity, defense and national security, education, general public services, social protection and social security, and healthcare. The budget allocates about 8.91 billion manat ($5.24 billion) to economic activity, roughly 8.82 billion manat ($5.19 billion) to defense and national security, 5.52 billion manat ($3.25 billion) to general public services, 5.99 billion manat ($3.52 billion) to education, 4.9 billion manat ($2.9 billion) to social protection and social security, and 2.8 billion manat ($1.6 billion) to healthcare. Of the education expenditure, 2.18 billion manat ($1.29 billion) will be allocated to general education, 434.8 million manat ($255.76 million) to preschool education, and 240.6 million manat ($141.53 million) to higher education. In healthcare, 1.1 billion manat ($647.06 million) is earmarked for the Compulsory Health Insurance Fund. A transfer of 1.6 billion manat ($941.18 million) from the state budget is allocated to balance the budget of the State Social Protection Fund. Under economic activity, 6.4 billion manat ($3.76 billion) will be allocated to construction and urban planning, including 5.3 billion manat ($3.1 billion) for public capital investment. Furthermore, about 1.38 billion manat ($811.47 million) is earmarked for agriculture, 438.6 million manat ($258 million) for environmental protection, and 335.2 million manat ($197.18 million) for housing and communal services. The ceiling on public debt servicing expenditure is set at 772.5 million manat ($454.41 million) for domestic debt and approximately 1.43 billion manat ($839.7 million) for external debt. These amounts include interest payments of 635.3 million manat ($373.71 million) and 364 million manat ($214 million), respectively. In 2027, the ceiling on domestic government borrowing is set at 2.5 billion manat ($1.47 billion), while the ceiling on external government borrowing is set at 6 billion manat ($3.53 billion). The ceiling on state guarantees to be issued during the year is also set at 6 billion manat. The state budget deficit of nearly 3.15 billion manat ($1.85 billion) is planned to be financed through privatization receipts, domestic and external borrowing, and the unspent balance in the single Treasury account as of January 1, 2027. For 2027, the ceiling on total consolidated budget expenditure is set at about 50.38 billion manat ($29.63 billion), while the ceiling on the consolidated budget deficit, excluding revenues of the relevant state institution, is set at approximately 16.7 billion manat ($9.8 billion). According to the draft law, the 2027 state budget law will enter into force on January 1, 2027. President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has instructed Chairman of the Agency for Atomic Energy Almasadam Satkaliyev to keep the development of national nuclear energy under special control, according to the presidential press service. The instruction followed a meeting with Satkaliyev, during which the head of state received a report on the agency’s key results for 2026. Tokayev was informed about the state of the nuclear industry and energy sector. In particular, the sides discussed the construction of nuclear power plants, the development of nuclear science and innovation, personnel training, and increasing the share of Kazakh content in industry projects. Special attention was paid to the creation of the Semipalatinsk nuclear safety zone, improvement of the radioactive waste management system, and strengthening of the regulatory framework in the field of nuclear and radiation safety. The president also instructed that timely measures be taken to implement the outlined tasks within the Strategy for the Development of the Nuclear Industry. A national referendum on the construction of a nuclear power plant in Kazakhstan was held on October 6, 2024. According to the results, 71.12% of citizens who took part in the vote supported the construction. By Government Resolution No. 1137 dated December 30, 2024, “On the construction area of the nuclear installation ‘Nuclear Power Plant’”, the Zhambyl district of the Almaty region was determined as the site for the first nuclear power plant. The plant will be built by Russia’s Rosatom. https://www.specialeurasia.com/2026/10/2.body: Armenian Constitutional Reform and Regional Peace Deal Armenian Constitutional Reform and Yerevan-Baku’s Peace Negotiations Image generated with the support of the artificial intelligence technology. Executive Intelligence Snapshot Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has framed Armenia’s proposed constitutional reform as a matter of domestic political choice and long-term state resilience, rejecting external interference while acknowledging Azerbaijan’s position on the issue in the context of bilateral peace negotiations. The government intends to secure opposition support for the reform; however, failure to reach a political consensus could prompt consideration of early parliamentary elections, increasing the importance of domestic political dynamics for the reform process and potentially affecting the wider peace agenda. Context On 22 October 2026 , Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that the authorities intend to publish a draft of the new Constitution in the near future and begin public discussions. However, he did not rule out holding early elections if the opposition fails to reach an agreement, and also admitted that his political mission could be exhausted if the people do not support his proposed agenda. Following the June 2026 parliamentary elections , Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s Civil Contract party secured 49.75% of the vote, enabling it to form a government independently. The result provides a parliamentary basis for pursuing the government’s agenda, although the ruling party does not hold the two-thirds majority required to initiate a constitutional referendum. The constitutional reform debate therefore remains politically significant, particularly given the opposition’s objections and the need to secure the necessary parliamentary support. The constitutional issue intersects with the Armenia–Azerbaijan normalisation process . At the Washington summit on 8 August 2025 , the two countries initialled the text of a peace agreement and committed to further steps towards its signature and ratification. The accompanying declaration also established a framework for developing the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity ( TRIPP ), a connectivity project through Armenian territory linking Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. Subsequent US–Armenian arrangements have advanced the project’s implementation framework. Baku has linked the constitutional issue to its position on a lasting peace settlement, while Pashinyan maintains that constitutional reform is a sovereign Armenian decision. This creates a political tension between Yerevan’s assertion of domestic ownership and the regional diplomatic context. Opposition claims that reform would amount to capitulation to Azerbaijani demands should be presented as an attributed political position, rather than an established consequence of the proposed changes. Drivers Political and security drivers . Pashinyan’s government presents constitutional reform as part of a wider effort to secure Armenia’s long-term state resilience and advance normalisation with Azerbaijan. Regional security concerns and the prospect of improved relations with Turkey form part of the broader strategic environment. Economic drivers . Reaching a deal with neighbouring Azerbaijan and restoring relations with Turkey might improve regional connectivity and reduce Armenia’s economic isolation, expand trade opportunities and attract investment. The US-backed TRIPP initiative is relevant because its proposed transport links could create economic opportunities while raising questions about sovereignty, jurisdiction and implementation. These benefits remain contingent on practical implementation and sustained regional stability. Societal drivers. Public debate over sovereignty, territorial integrity, the peace settlement and the treatment of displaced Armenians from Nagorno-Karabakh may constrain the government’s room for manoeuvre. Risk and Strategic Implications The primary risk is that failure to secure sufficient political support for constitutional reform could intensify domestic polarisation, weaken the government’s capacity to implement its political agenda and complicate progress towards normalisation with Azerbaijan. Pashinyan’s reference to possible early parliamentary elections introduces an additional source of uncertainty . A deterioration in bilateral relations or a slowdown in the peace process is a plausible second-order consequence, particularly if either government treats the constitutional dispute as an obstacle to further negotiations. Successful constitutional reform could enable Pashinyan to advance his state-building agenda and reinforce his political narrative that normalisation with Azerbaijan is necessary for Armenia’s long-term security and prosperity. For Baku, constitutional change would address a central stated condition for signing the initialled peace agreement, although it would not by itself guarantee the agreement’s signature, ratification or implementation. Conversely, failure to secure the required support could provide opposition parties with an opportunity to challenge the government’s approach to peace and constitutional reform, particularly if early parliamentary elections follow. Parties advocating closer relations with Russia could gain political visibility from such a setback; however, any resulting shift in Armenia’s external alignment would depend on electoral outcomes, coalition dynamics and subsequent policy decisions, rather than follow automatically from a failed reform process. Conclusion Pashinyan is likely to continue presenting constitutional reform as a component of Yerevan’s long-term state resilience and regional normalisation agenda. The government may seek to build political and public support through consultations and engagement with opposition representatives, while retaining early elections as a possible alternative if consensus proves unattainable. Azerbaijan is likely to maintain its stated position on constitutional change as part of the peace process, while monitoring developments in Armenia’s domestic political debate. Opposition parties may continue challenging the government’s approach and arguing that constitutional reform entails unacceptable concessions to Baku. The immediate trajectory will depend on whether the government publishes the draft Constitution, initiates consultations and secures meaningful parliamentary engagement. Через три месяца приговорили к трём годам лишения свободы, вскоре помиловали. С 2003 года Фарид Тухбатуллин живет в Австрии. Он является соучредителем «Туркменской инициативы по правам человека». Недавно швейцарское издательство Sandermoen Publishing выпустило его книгу «Российская колония: туркменские саги». Ранее Фарид Тухбатуллин печатался в британском журнале Index on Censorship. Он также был среди инициаторов и авторов сборника современных туркменских литераторов « У оврага... за последними домами » (2015). Как память и литература влияют на судьбу? Чем сегодня живет Туркменистан и политические беженцы из этой страны? Этот опыт важен для противников любой диктатуры, в том числе для российской политической эмиграции. Туркменский правозащитник ответил на вопросы редакции «Швейцария для всех». От эколога до писателя — Как эколог стал правозащитником, правозащитник — политзаключённым, а политзаключённый — писателем? После окончания сельскохозяйственного института в Ашхабаде я в 1980-х работал в системе Министерства водного хозяйства Туркменистана. При Горбачеве стали открыто говорить об усыхании Аральского моря и сопутствующих экологических проблемах. Северную часть Туркменистана, где я родился и жил, включили в кризисную зону. По статистике, у нас была самая высокая в СССР детская и материнская смертность. Тогда с единомышленниками мы и стали заниматься общественной деятельностью в защиту экологии. Параллельно в стране устанавливалась диктатура. И я нелегально занялся сбором фактов о нарушениях прав человека, передавал эти сведения в Московское отделение «Мемориала». Участвовал за рубежом в правозащитных конференциях, семинарах, тренингах. Затем были арест, осуждение, помилование и эмиграция. Этот опыт частично вошел в мою книгу. — В книге « Российская колония: туркменские саги » переплетены легенды, мифы, мистика и документальная проза. У звёзд есть гнёзда. Где для вас проходит граница между реальностью и вымыслом? — Я хотел рассказать о реальных событиях и туркменской культуре, дорогой мне и малоизвестной миру, ведь настоящее и прошлое неразделимы. В основе традиционной туркменской мифологии — древний тюркский эпический мир, соединившийся с доисламскими верованиями и исламской традицией. Один из центральных пластов — предания об Огуз-хане, легендарном прародителе огузских племён. Другой важнейший памятник — «Книга моего деда Коркута» («Китаби Деде Коркут»), цикл сказаний о героях, роде, верности, войне, смерти и судьбе. В древнем мифологическом слое важны волк, конь, птицы, дерево, вода, пустыня и гора. Волк может быть проводником и прародителем, конь — спутником и почти продолжением героя. Мир духов, пери и дивов соседствует с исламскими представлениями о джиннах, святых и чудесах. Древние сакральные места после исламизации могли почитаться уже как связанные с новыми святыми. Важнейшая часть традиции — героический эпос «Гёроглы» («Кёроглы»), в котором герой становится воплощением сопротивления, справедливости и свободы. Поэтому на страницах моей книги и живут волки, вороны, Бездна, Бог, предания и голоса умерших. За ними стоит культура, веками сохранявшая историческую память через эпос, родовые предания и устный рассказ. — Насколько отличаются устная память и официальная история Туркменистана? Кто решает, что людям помнить, что забыть? Советская пропаганда семьдесят лет извращала туркменскую историю. Исторические личности, защищавшие свою землю, традиции, веру, стали отрицательными персонажами. А люди, которые переметнулись к большевикам, то есть фактически стали предателями своей культуры и народа, почитались советской властью как герои. Эта подмена жива в памяти многих туркмен и в наше время. После обретения независимости власти поначалу пытались исправить официальную политику памяти. Но быстро поняли, что на фоне реальных героев, сражавшихся против Российской империи, а затем и с большевиками, героическая биография Туркменбаши соткана слишком грубо — подмена видна в самом узоре. Туркменистан обрел независимость в результате распада СССР, заслуги Ниязова тут нет. А он при жизни ставил памятники себе и своим родным. Пришедшие ему на смену поступают так же. — В названии «Российская колония» читается и колония империи, и место заключения. Чувствуете ли вы связь с традицией лагерной литературы, например, с прозой Шаламова? — Название книги я выбрал осознанно. Что касается прозы Шаламова, возможно, в главе «Сто и одна ночь при свете лампочки» есть такая связь. Как и он, я старался тоже не указывать, кто хороший, а кто плохой. Просто описывал ситуацию и реакцию тех или иных персонажей. — Обвинения в покушении на Ниязова, тюрьма... О чём труднее говорить — о насилии столетней давности или о пережитом лично? — О пережитом лично. Наверное, поэтому книге, чтобы появиться, потребовалось почти двадцать лет. Туркменская правозащита — Что можно рассказать о работе туркменских правозащитников, которые наблюдают за нарушением прав и свобод человека в Туркменистане? Как это начиналось? — После провозглашения независимости Туркменистана в 1991 году возможности для независимого наблюдения за соблюдением прав человека быстро сокращались. Уже в начале 1990-х правозащитная деятельность существовала главным образом как работа отдельных активистов, диссидентов и представителей немногочисленных общественных объединений, а не легально действующих специализированных организаций. Human Rights Watch отмечала , что к 1993 году число людей, открыто критиковавших власть, сократилось с нескольких тысяч в конце 1980-х до нескольких десятков. Правозащитники и оппозиционные активисты подвергались задержаниям, допросам, слежке, ограничениям на выезд, увольнениям, давление распространялось и на родственников. В условиях, когда собственно правозащитные объединения практически не могли существовать, частью независимого гражданского наблюдения становились экологические, культурные и другие общественные инициативы. Один из примеров — Дашогузский экологический клуб, к которому я присоединился в 1993 году и впоследствии стал его сопредседателем. Мы занимались не только экологией. Создали и поддерживали в 1995–1998 годах независимую общественную библиотеку, а в 2001–2002 годах организовали центр поддержки гражданских инициатив. Я одновременно участвовал в мониторинге положения с правами человека и сотрудничал с международными правозащитными структурами. Власть это раздражало. Одна из главных задач туркменских активистов заключалась уже не только в публичном протесте, но и в сборе информации и передаче её наружу — за пределы страны: сведений о задержанных, заключённых, судебных процессах, давлении на семьи и ограничении основных свобод. Закрытость страны одновременно делала такую информацию особенно ценной и чрезвычайно опасной для её источников. Между легендой и тюрьмой — Покушение на Ниязова произошло 25 ноября 2002 года. Насильственная смена власти — не редкость при диктатурах. У участников событий было оружие? — В книге есть описание, как они готовились, накануне вечером привезли оружие, и оно было при них на следующее утро. Затем последовали массовые аресты, закрытые судебные процессы и сообщения о пытках. По данным Международной Хельсинкской федерации по правам человека (МХФ) и «Мемориала», не менее 200 человек были задержаны, более 100 — обвинены. Власти официально сообщали о 67 арестованн

https://www.rferl.org/a/roghun-dam-tajik.body: Tajikistan The Rise Of Roghun: 'World's Tallest' Dam Takes Shape In Tajikistan October 21, 2026 18:23 CET By Amos Chapple Photo: Webuild Image Library (Courtesy Image) Tajikistan The Rise Of Roghun: 'World's Tallest' Dam Takes Shape In Tajikistan October 21, 2026 18:23 CET By Amos Chapple The Rise Of Roghun: 'World's Tallest' Dam Takes Shape In Tajikistan Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google A Soviet-era plan to build the world's tallest dam edged closer to reality this month as international lenders step up support for Tajikistan's Roghun hydropower project. In early October Dushanbe ratified a $300 million grant from the World Bank for the project and reports have since emerged of a possible further $500 million in funding from the Asian Development Bank. Filippo Menga , an associate professor of geography at the University of Bergamo in Italy, told RFE/RL the recent funding news doesn't assure the project's completion, but with major multilateral banks tying their own credibility to Roghun, "financially and politically the project is now very hard to stop," he said. A cavern in the Roghun Dam under construction in 2019 The Roghun Dam project is set to rise 335 meters -- higher than the Eiffel Tower -- to plug a narrow gorge of the Vakhsh River 100 kilometers east of Dushanbe. The hydropower plant will double Tajikistan's generating capacity, potentially ending the country's chronic winter electricity shortages , and providing surplus power for export. The massive dam will also displace more than 50,000 people as water rises to fill its reservoir, inundating several villages upstream of the project. Interactive embed: Rogun Dam Flooding In a village near Roghun, Mukim Khasanov was one of the tens of thousands of people awaiting resettlement when RFE/RL's Tajik Service spoke to him in June. The 75-year-old farmer said his family were allocated a plot of land away from the dam but that inflation will devour much of the compensation for his house that was promised years earlier. "When they assessed our housing and property, prices were completely different, including for building materials," he said. "Now everything is very expensive. For example, a wood panel cost 50 somoni (about $5.40) back then, and now it's 150 somoni (about $16.30)." In Roghunyon, a suburb on the outskirts of Dushanbe named to reference the origin of many villagers already relocated from the reservoir's flood zone, some complain the land promised to them for growing crops never eventuated. Others express "100 percent satisfaction" with the settlement. "No problems whatsoever," Tavakkal Shamsulloev said. "They've repaired our roads and installed electricity." A former village 15 kilometers northeast of the Roghun Dam has been cleared of people and structures as part of an ongoing resettlement program to make way for the dam. Opponents of the dam project have claimed some 32,000 people would be able to avoid resettlement if the dam were to be built just 35 meters lower. Eugene Simonov, the coordinator of the conservation coalition Rivers Without Boundaries , told RFE/RL it appears likely Dushanbe has pursued the title of the tallest dam in the world as "an important quality of the national pride project akin to a sacred pyramid," for the country. Dushanbe has said the record-breaking height will offer "superior economic and environmental performance" compared to lower versions of the dam. That assessment has been backed by World Bank reports. Work under way on a tunnel amid construction of the Roghun dam in 1987 The Roghun Dam was initially envisioned by the Soviet Union and work began in 1976. Amid the breakup of the USSR, followed by civil war in Tajikistan, the project collapsed. Efforts by newly independent Tajikistan to restart the project were initially opposed by Uzbekistan, which lies downstream of the dam. Uzbekistan's then President Islam Karimov slammed the Roghun Dam as "stupid," citing safety concerns and fears Tajikistan could use its control of water flowing toward Uzbekistan for political leverage. Workers seen on a road near the Roghun construction site in April 1981 Uzbekistan's opposition to the dam evaporated following the death of Karimov in 2016. The following year, Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Abdulaziz Komilov publicly invited Tajikistan to "go ahead and build" the dam, while insisting on guarantees regarding water use. Construction resumed later that year , but the site proved immensely complex. A meters-wide vein of rock salt just upstream of the dam risked dissolving under pressure of a rising water reservoir, and the dam's location in a seismically restless region introduced the potential for "reservoir-triggered" quakes, according to multiple technical reports. Additionally, the Soviet-era work on the project was found to require extensive rebuilding to meet modern safety standards. Webuild, the Italian infrastructure giant working on the project, declined to comment on technical aspects of the build, but a 2014 report describes "substantial remedial works" needed on Soviet construction efforts. Roghun is being built as an embankment dam, incorporating a core of watertight clay buttressed on both sides by rockfill. The relatively flexible dam type was chosen in part for its capacity to absorb quakes better than crackable concrete-faced dams. Two of the hydropower plant's turbines are already in operation, with the third of a total of six generating units s cheduled to come online in 2027. A section of the Roghun Dam under construction in 2024 Menga, who has authored a book on water politics in Central Asia, says that with around 145 meters left to build up the dam and its completion requiring continued political goodwill from Tajikistan's Central Asian neighbors, "Roghun is more likely to be finished than ever before, but 'virtually assured' overstates it." The Tajik government is estimated to still require around $5.8 billion to complete the Roghun hydropower project, which will be funded largely from the country's state budget. The target completion date is 2035. WASHINGTON -- Ukraine has yet to receive answers from the Pentagon or Elon Musk's SpaceX over restrictions on satellite communications used by its military, Kyiv's top diplomat in Washington told RFE/RL, as a growing bipartisan push for a congressional investigation intensified. "Speed restrictions have not been lifted," Denys Sienik, Ukraine's charge d'affaires in the United States, told RFE/RL on October 21, adding Kyiv had received no response from either the Pentagon or SpaceX. The dispute over Starlink and its military-oriented counterpart, Starshield, has raised questions about who authorized the restrictions, whether the Trump administration knew about them in advance, and how the changes affected Ukraine's ability to defend against Russian attacks. On October 21, Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that President Donald Trump or anyone in the US government had requested changes to the systems. But a congressional delegation that recently visited Kyiv said the restrictions had impaired Ukrainian air defenses and put American personnel at risk. SEE ALSO: After Witkoff Meeting, Putin 'Ready To Resume' US-Led Peace Talks With Ukraine Disruptions to the Starshield satellite system, the military-grade version of the Starlink service operated by SpaceX on which Kyiv heavily relies to defend against Russian air strikes, has left Ukraine particularly vulnerable since they were first reported on October 13-14. Russia Launches Fresh Ukraine Attacks Russia launched fresh attacks on Kyiv in three waves of ballistic missile strikes overnight on October 22, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, just hours after US special envoy Steve Witkoff held talks on moving the peace process forward with Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom he described as a "humanitarian." The strikes on the capital hit residential buildings, energy facilities, infrastructure at a railway station and the metro, shopping malls, businesses, and a monastery, Zelenskyy wrote on X. He added that Russia had launched 21 missiles at Ukraine, leaving two people confirmed dead and 34 others injured, including five children, in Kyiv and across the regions. Russia Hits Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles by RFE/RL No media source currently available 0:00 0:00:33 0:00 "Overnight, Kyiv residents heard what Russian 'humanism' truly sounds like," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha wrote on X . "Appeasement, servility, and flattery will not stop this war. Only strength will," he added. Witkoff described Putin as a "humanitarian" on October 22 after the Kremlin released US citizen Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old former school teacher, after spending more than four years in detention in Russia following a conviction for mercenary activity ⁠in a closed-door trial. His family has disputed the charge. Meanwhile, Russia's Defense Ministry reported its air defenses destroyed over 800 Ukrainian drones overnight, including 630 heading toward the Moscow region, while Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 163 drones were intercepted near the capital. Air Defenses Impaired Dan Rice, a former special adviser to the commander in chief of Ukraine's armed forces and current president of American University Kyiv, told RFE/RL that several separate issues had become entangled in the controversy: intelligence-sharing, satellite speed restrictions, and deliveries of Patriot air-defense interceptors. Rice said he believed Rubio was referring to intelligence-sharing when he insisted the United States had not interrupted assistance to Ukraine. "The intel was shared," Rice said, adding that a technical glitch had prevented air-raid alerts from reaching people's phones. "If Secretary Rubio says there was no interruption of intel -- I believe him." The distinction matters because continued intelligence-sharing does not necessarily mean satellite connectivity was unaffected. SEE ALSO: Uncertainty Over US Intelligence To Ukraine As Russia Pounds Kyiv During an October 21 briefing, a Senate Democratic aide who had recently returned from Kyiv said the delegation witnessed Russian drones and missiles approaching the capital with unusually limited advance warning. The aide said the Starshield restrictions were in effect during the October 13-16 visit and that the delegation's assessment was they had endangered both Ukrainian civilians and US personnel. Russian jet-powered Shahed drones, which can travel at 280 miles per hour or faster, have posed a particular challenge. Starshield speed limits were reportedly initially set at about 60 miles per hour and later at 100 miles per hour, meaning the system could lose connectivity with faster-moving objects. Rubio Denies US Role Speaking in Mumbai on October 21, Rubio stressed that Starlink and Starshield are separate systems. Starlink is a commercial satellite-Internet service that can also be used to guide drones, he said, while Starshield is a specialized defense product sold and operated through the US Defense Department. Rubio said he had not read The Wall Street Journal report alleging that Musk ordered the slowdown. He denied Trump or other US officials had requested changes or had advance knowledge of the decision. SEE ALSO: Rubio Vows To Keep Pushing For Ukraine Peace, Seeks Deeper US Ties In Central Asia Neither "the president of the United States nor anyone in our system ever requested that any changes to that system be made," Rubio said. He argued that the government could not dictate how a private company manages a commercial product, while acknowledging that Starshield operates under different arrangements because it is procured for government use. Congress Demands Answers Democrats and some Republicans have called for investigations into the slowdown. Senator Adam Schiff of California said in a social media post the conflicting accounts warranted a full Senate investigation and called for Musk to testify under oath. Senator Ruben Gallego of Arizona also urged Musk to explain the decision voluntarily. Senator Chris Coons of Delaware said Musk should not have the power to influence the outcome of a war "with the flip of a switch," while Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts warned of the risks of a private executive effectively dictating US foreign policy. Representative Ami Bera, a California Democrat, said the slowdown had "crippled Ukrainian defenses and endangered innocent lives," calling on Congress to establish who authorized it and hold those responsible accountable. Republican Representative Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania has also called for an investigation. "If Ukraine cannot reliably intercept Russian 'arrows,' it must be able to shoot the 'archer,'" the lawmakers wrote in a letter sent on October 21, arguing that Ukraine needs the ability to destroy the launchers used to attack its cities. The initiative was led by Republican Representative Joe Wilson of South Carolina and included seven Republicans and 16 Democrats. The lawmakers said granting Ukraine greater access could save lives and give Russian President Vladimir Putin greater incentives to negotiate. https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-moldova-.body: Moldova Amid Russia's Onslaught, A Twist In The Pursuit Of Men Fleeing Ukraine For Moldova By RFE/RL's Moldovan Service October 21, 2026 17:35 CET Amid Russia's Onslaught, A Twist In The Pursuit Of Men Fleeing Ukraine For Moldova Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Screenshots from a video show Ukrainian border guards in a boat on the Moldovan side of the Dniester River and a Ukrainian man in the water next to them on October 15. The video, apparently shot by a bystander, was posted on social media by the small right-wing parliamentary opposition party Democracy At Home. The footage is blurry but dramatic: Two camouflage-clad men in a motor-powered dinghy circle a third individual who is struggling in the water, shouting and grabbing at him. At one point, one of them men tries to hit the swimmer repeatedly with an oar. The scene played out in the middle of the Dniester River, which winds along a stretch of the border between Moldova and Ukraine and is used as a crossing by Ukrainians trying to flee their country as Russia's full-scale war rages on toward the five-year mark. Ukraine is scrambling to alleviate a manpower shortage that is hurting its defense against a much more populous attacker. As in Russia, recruiters in Ukraine have sometimes used forceful methods to round up men to fight. SEE ALSO: Ukraine’s Western Front: Hunting Draft Dodgers On The Romanian Border Most men aged 23-60 are forbidden to leave the country. Many have tried to cross into Moldova or neighboring Romania , sometimes risking their lives on potentially treacherous rivers. At least twice this month, there's been a new twist: Ukrainian border guards giving chase to compatriots have ended up on the Moldovan side and been detained by their Moldovan counterparts. That's what happened in the case purportedly captured on a bystander's video on October 15. After the fray in the river, the guards are seen sitting in the dinghy on shore in Moldova and an expletive-laden exchange ensues, in Russian, with people berating them for their treatment of the fugitive. Local residents pulled the man out of the river and he was hospitalized, according to Moldovan media reports. Reports identified him as Oleksiy Koval, a 49-year-old clinical psychologist from Kyiv, and said he was trying to reach his family, who had left Ukraine earlier. Officials said he applied for asylum in Moldova, which means he is highly unlikely to be sent back to Ukraine. Many of the Ukrainians fleeing across the border into Moldova rely on smuggling networks operating on both sides that charge fees to sneak them across. Cooperation between the two countries focuses primarily on dismantling these networks. SEE ALSO: Moldovan Parliament Denounces Russian 'Genocide' In Ukraine However, once Ukrainian men reach Moldovan soil and apply for asylum, the law effectively prevents their repatriation: Authorities are not allowed to send applicants back if there are "reasonable grounds to believe" their lives would be in danger or they would risk being subjected to torture or other inhuman or degrading treatment. According to Moldovan government statistics, in the first four years of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine -- from February 2022 to March 2026 -- about 44,000 Ukrainians, mostly men, were caught illegally crossing the border into Moldova. Most moved on to other countries in Europe. 'Extreme Cruelty' A few days after the two incidents, the Ukrainian border guards were released and sent back. But the drama on the river has set off political reverberations in Moldova, where President Maia Sandu's pro-Western government is a vocal supporter of Ukraine in its defense against Russia. The October 15 incident was first brought to light by Democracy At Home, a small right-wing parliamentary opposition party that published the video before Moldovan authorities made a statement about the matter. In a video post, party leader Vasile Costiuc criticized the Moldovan state's decision to repatriate the Ukrainian guards and said the authorities "lack a unified stance on such a vital matter as state security." Democracy at Home called on the Foreign Ministry to issue a note of protest to Kyiv. It urged Sandu to "refuse to tolerate the repeated violations of the state border" and to decorate two residents of from the riverside village of Holoșnița for "civic heroism," claiming they had saved the life of the Ukrainian man. The main opposition group, the Party of Socialists (PSRM), which advocates closer ties with Russia, called the Ukrainian border guards' actions a case of "extreme cruelty" that reveals "the true face of the Kyiv regime, the closest partner and 'friend' of Maia Sandu." Socialist leader Igor Dodon, a Moscow-friendly former president who lost to Sandu in a 2020 election, accused her administration of turning Moldova into a "free transit zone for foreign special services." SEE ALSO: More Drones, More Missiles, No Air Defenses: Moldova In The Cross Fire Of Russia's War On Ukraine The party formally requested answers from the government on the Ukrainian guards' border incursion and the legal basis under which they were released and sent back to Ukraine rather than being detained on suspicion of attempted murder. Ruling Action and Solidarity Party (PAS) lawmaker Lilian Carp, head of the parliamentary national-security committee, said that "nothing justifies such behavior from border guards." Speaking on public broadcaster Moldova 1, he also claimed the Foreign Ministry had sent a note of protest to Kyiv regarding the October 15 incident. The ministry flatly denied that, saying the matter was "being addressed through institutional communication channels between the competent authorities." 'Grateful To Ukraine' Ukraine's Border Guard Service said it had opened an investigation into the reports and the actions of the border patrol involved. It said the guards ended up on Moldovan territory because the water level was low and the boat's outboard motor failed during the pursuit. Prime Minister Vasile Tofan argued that Moldovan authorities acted responsibly and such incidents must be viewed in the context of Moscow's war, saying they would not happen if Russia was not attacking Ukraine. "I am very grateful to Ukraine for defending both us and Europe," he said. Moldova's security has been compromised in various ways by Russia's war. Dozens of drones and missiles launched by Russia have crashed in Moldova, which is bordered by Ukraine on three sides, and the frequency of these incidents has increased in recent months. Last week, following an investigation by RFE/RL's Moldovan Service , the government announced an investigation into concerns that Russian tech giant Yandex has been harvesting Moldovans' personal data by sending it directly to servers in Russia. https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2.body: Responding to the latest acts of state-driven Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank over the weekend, which also targeted a delegation of European diplomats and a Washington Post photojournalist, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, Heba Morayef, said: “Once again, Israel’s apartheid system is turning the olive harvest into a season of horror for Palestinian families across the occupied West Bank. State-driven attacks by settlers on farmers that damage, destroy and steal crops, combined with Israeli military restrictions on access to groves, are causing immense suffering and economic loss for Palestinians. “The series of attacks by settlers over the weekend against Palestinian residents of Khirbet Abu Falah and Taybeh in the Ramallah area, which also targeted a Washington Post photojournalist and a delegation of European diplomats, offer a glimpse into a reality of relentless aggression against Palestinians. Attempts by senior Israeli officials and electoral candidates across the political spectrum to portray this state-sponsored brutality as the work of a few individuals are a blatant distortion of reality. “Amnesty International has long been sounding the alarm over the exponential rise in state-driven settler violence against Palestinians, which has sought, through terror-inspiring means, to ethnically cleanse Palestinians from the occupied West Bank. This rise of violence has been fuelled by the international community’s persistent failure to take meaningful action against the very system enabling the continued oppression of Palestinians. These attacks must generate a strong response by states that claim to oppose Israel’s annexation of Palestinian territory, its continuous settlement expansion and state-driven settler violence. “States must recognize that settler attacks are not isolated acts, but a central policy of the Israeli state and take concrete measures to respect their obligations under international law and to avoid complicity in Israeli violations and crimes against Palestinians by halting all trade, investment and cooperation that contribute to maintaining the unlawful occupation, apartheid and the ongoing campaign of ethnic cleansing. “States must also impose targeted sanctions against Israeli officials credibly implicated in serious violations of international law and support international justice and accountability efforts. Hiding behind empty rhetoric is not only cowardly, it is enabling further abuses. For Palestinians, it continues to be deadly.” Background On 16 October, dozens of masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian farmers harvesting olives near the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah. During the attack, settlers reportedly threw stones, used slingshots, set olive trees on fire and assaulted Palestinians. US photojournalist Heidi Levine, who was covering the olive harvest for The Washington Post, was knocked to the ground, and repeatedly kicked despite wearing clearly marked press protective gear. She also had her camera equipment and phone stolen, and was hospitalized with multiple injuries. On 19 October, Israeli police said they had arrested 10 suspects as part of an investigation into the incidents. The following day masked Israeli settlers attacked a group that included Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, a French mayor, Catholic representatives and Palestinian residents near the village of Taybeh, also northeast of Ramallah. A Belgian diplomatic vehicle was also reportedly damaged and several members of the delegation were assaulted. Amnesty International’s 2026 report on the occupied West Bank documented how since late 2022 Israeli authorities have escalated a state-led and state-sponsored campaign of ethnic cleansing, terrorizing and forcibly displacing thousands of Palestinians from Bedouin and herding communities in Area C of the West Bank to permanently alter its demography. In pursuing their goal of formal annexation, they have accelerated settlement expansion, intensified movement restrictions, exponentially increased funding as well as logistical, legal and political support to settlements and outposts, distributed arms to settlers and openly encouraged, facilitated, and condoned settler attacks as a deliberate tool of displacement. Palestinian communities across the occupied West Bank have faced a sharp increase in settler attacks since October 2023 aimed at forcibly displacing them through physical assaults, threats and harassment against individuals; destruction of property, arson, crop theft; restrictions on access to agricultural and grazing land; and acts of theft and harm against livestock. Amnesty International is calling on states to suspend all forms of cooperation that contribute to maintaining Israel’s unlawful occupation, ban trade with Israeli settlements, impose targeted sanctions against Israeli officials directly implicated in Israel’s ethnic cleansing campaign and serious crimes under international law against Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, impose a comprehensive embargo on arms and security equipment to Israel, and support international accountability mechanisms, including ongoing investigations by the International Criminal Court.

Abu Suleiman is the Head of the Local Council from Zanuta , a village in the South Hebron Hills in the southern occupied West Bank. He, along with all 250 Zanuta residents, has been forcibly displaced from the village for three years as a result of Israel’s ethnic cleansing campaign targeting Palestinian Bedouin and herding communities in Area C. Zanuta, my village, never, ever leaves my thoughts. Now, I live in Al-Dhahiriya, a stone’s throw away from Zanuta. But between me and Zanuta stand Israeli settlers, checkpoints, outposts and soldiers, reinforced by [the authorities’] lack of will to implement a court order. Every time I step outside the house I now live in, I look toward Zanuta. It is right there in front of me. There is hardly a week that goes by without me dreaming about Zanuta. We lived in Zanuta, as did our fathers and grandfathers. Then suddenly, in 2020, a settler appears and starts telling us: “This land is mine.” We were born in this area, so all our experiences, both good and bad, took place there. Our memories are there. Our livelihood, our sheep, our land, our crops, our farming. The exhaustion of herding the sheep, taking them across long distances, being out in the rain. Everything is in Zanuta. We lived there despite the harsh conditions. Even the hardship of living there and the things that used to annoy me, I now long for. Before we were displaced, there were no services, no proper roads and no electricity in Zanuta. We only had electricity from solar panels provided by a local NGO. It was a very basic way of life. Yet despite all that, we were living on our land, in our homes. There may have been barracks and tents, but we were living a simple, beautiful and dignified life with peace of mind on our own land, in our own village. The Israeli military does nothing We tried to stay, but in the end, everyone reaches a breaking point. People fear for their lives, their children, their livelihoods, and their flocks. That is only natural. Israeli settlers came to Zanuta in 2020. They were taking over grazing lands, harassing people, seizing wells and water sources, intimidating residents, even attacking livestock. In 2021, they established an illegal outpost just 1km away known as Meitarim Farm. These abuses existed before 7 October 2023, but since then, the state-backed settler violence has intensified dramatically and the campaign has become much more aggressive across the West Bank, especially in Area C, including Zanuta and Masafer Yatta. We, the residents of Zanuta, did not remain silent. We pursued legal action and obtained rulings from the Israeli High Court of Justice ordering the military and police to facilitate our return and to protect us against settler violence. The Israeli army has failed to implement the decision of the court, though. We tried to return, but to no avail. The major obstacle preventing people from returning is the herding outpost of Meitarim: most of the attacks against us come from that outpost and instead of preventing those attacks, the Israeli military does nothing. A heavy burden Zanuta never leaves our minds, not day or night. It is our land and our home. We have not attacked anyone. We are ordinary people who live from our herds, our livelihoods, our homes, and our simple way of life. We did not voluntarily leave our land as some believe. The pain of displacement and forced expulsion is a heavy burden. It feels as if, after everything, we are being punished for something that was never our fault. Our children were happy. They used to play and roam freely with the sheep in the open land and fields of Zanuta. They had a school and a kindergarten. But now they live in a different environment in Al-Dhahiriya. It may have bigger houses and more services, but it is different than where they came from and has affected them psychologically. Not to mention that witnessing settlers carrying weapons and driving through the area deeply affected and frightened them. They still have nightmares. My 73-year-old mother, like many other older women from Zanuta, chokes with tears when she recalls the village. Our families, who once lived decently in Zanuta, are left without employment opportunities and with no space to keep their livestock. Now people must rent land, buy metal fencing, and cover additional costs. Families have had to sell sheep to buy food, both for their animals and for themselves. Today, it feels as though no one is listening to us anymore. Since we were displaced, very few people have reached out to help us. My cousin, a husband and a father of six, used to work and support his family, and he also owned sheep. Since the displacement, he has fallen into severe depression and is taking medication. He has stopped working entirely. He barely speaks. One of his sons works as a driver, but there is very little business. The family struggles to get by. Help ensure the implementation of the court’s decisions Our request is simple. There are court rulings that already exist in the case of Zanuta. We ask the world to pressure Israel to respect and implement the decisions of its own courts. That is our primary demand; to go home – and to ensure accountability for all the injustice we have gone through. Communities in Area C, which makes up around 60 per cent of the West Bank, deserve sustained international attention and protection. We ask people of conscience, people of goodwill around the world to stand with us, international media to come and report on our situation and diplomatic delegations to visit the area and maintain a presence on the ground. Increased attention and pressure on the Israeli government can help ensure the implementation of the court’s decisions. I can picture myself walking through the village. I remember where the houses were, where we took the sheep, our lands, how we grazed them, where we drove the tractor, where the wells were. Every detail stays with me. It only leaves me when I sleep, and when I sleep, I dream about it. In a recent report , Amnesty International demonstrated that the ethnic cleansing campaign is not the product of “rogue” settlers but an integral part of an organized state policy. Take action to demand that the Israeli authorities immediately ensure the safe return of Zanuta’s residents to their lands Sign our petition to stop Israel’s ethnic cleansing in the West Bank

The Sri Lankan government’s proposed new counterterrorism legislation allows wide scope for abuse and poses serious threats to human rights, said Amnesty International in a new legal analysis. Despite some improvements on the previous white paper of the law issued in late 2025, the Protection of the State from Terrorism bill, which will replace the repressive and long-standing Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), retains an overly broad and ambiguous definition of terrorism that leaves room for arbitrary interpretation and the potential criminalization of dissent, protest, and the activities of civil society organizations. The bill, which was tabled on 6 October, is now before the Supreme Court to check its compatibility with Sri Lanka’s Constitution. Depending on the Supreme Court’s determination, the law is set to be debated by Sri Lanka’s parliament in the coming weeks. “Any attempt to revise a counterterror law which has time and time again been weaponized by the authorities against dissent, government critics, and minorities must be given the utmost scrutiny. The new bill must break with this legacy of abuse, not give the authorities new tools to silence dissent,” said Smriti Singh, Amnesty International’s South Asia Director. Sri Lanka’s history of abusing such legislation makes robust, enforceable safeguards essential Smriti Singh, Amnesty International’s South Asia Director “ Sri Lanka’s history of abusing such legislation makes robust, enforceable safeguards essential, and these remain inadequately addressed in the bill, sparking serious human rights concerns.” In addition to the overbroad definition of terrorism, the bill permits detention for up to one year without charge, alongside the possibility of up to one year of pretrial detention – a cumulation of two years in detention even before the start of a trial. This breaches the right to be free from arbitrary detention, the presumption of innocence, and the right to be tried within a reasonable time. “Allowing a person to be detained for up to a year before being charged, with the prospect of a further year in pretrial detention, raises grave concerns about arbitrary detention and the right to a fair trial. No one should have to spend years in detention while the state delays bringing a case to trial,” said Smriti Singh. “We urge Sri Lanka’s parliament to withdraw this bill and reform the law in line with international human rights law and standards. Until this is done, the PTA should not be misused further.” Amnesty International is calling on Sri Lanka’s authorities to reform the law using key benchmarks provided to Sri Lanka by UN special rapporteurs to enable substantive reform of the PTA. Offence of terrorism remains too broad The bill’s definition of terrorism is narrower compared with the bill’s earlier draft and incorporates additional safeguards. For example, the initial draft criminalized certain acts done with the purpose of “infringing on the sovereignty of Sri Lanka”, without a clear definition of what would constitute such intent. This has been removed in the updated bill, which is welcome. However, Amnesty International is concerned that the offence of terrorism, as drafted in the bill, remains too broad and falls below the standards required under international law. Firstly, section 3(4) of the bill does not expressly exclude protests, advocacy, dissent, industrial action, or humanitarian and medical assistance from the scope of terrorism offences. Instead, it merely states that such conduct is not, by itself, sufficient to establish the required elements of an offence. This caveat falls short of a clear safeguard as it leaves room for broad interpretation. The law should clearly state that protected activities, such as protests and advocacy, cannot be treated as terrorism offences. Secondly, Amnesty International does not consider that offences only causing a “likelihood” of “substantial economic loss”, as laid down in the new bill, meet the high hurt threshold required for an offence to constitute terrorism. Significant human rights issues persist The tabled bill introduces various new safeguards compared to the 2025 white paper. These include judicial oversight of any attempt by the Executive to proscribe an organization and the establishment of a review committee to examine the legality of detention orders. However, the committee’s members will be appointed by the Minister of Defence, a member of the cabinet, raising serious questions about its independence. A review committee appointed by a minister cannot provide the necessary assurance of independent scrutiny Smriti Singh “A review committee appointed by a minister cannot provide the necessary assurance of independent scrutiny of detention orders. It is the criminal justice system, with the safeguards of a fair criminal trial, that should determine whether a person is guilty of a crime and should be sentenced,” said Smriti Singh. Other human rights concerns around the bill raised previously by Amnesty International remain. These include the extension of police powers to armed forces and coast guards; as well as provisions permitting the Attorney General, with High Court approval, to defer prosecutions or suspend trials for up to 20 years in certain cases. Rather than proceeding to trial, suspects may agree to conditions such as apologies or reparations, while remaining exposed to the prospect of prosecution for decades. This raises concerns regarding accountability, victims’ right to justice, and the right of accused persons to legal certainty and a timely determination of criminal charges. Background The PTA has historically been used to target minorities, civic dissent and has continued being misused by the current administration for prolonged detention of drug-related crime suspects. The PTA, which the current government pledged to repeal, is not only still in the books, but still very much in use (OHCHR received information from the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka that it had been notified of 46 PTA-related detention cases in 2025 and 12 cases as of March 2026), despite calls for a moratorium. Amnesty has consistently called for the repeal of the PTA and a moratorium on the use of the act in the meantime. The organization raised concerns about the earlier draft of the Protection of the State from Terrorism bill in March 2026 .

Responding to the news that Lina Atallah, editor-in-chief of independent outlet Mada Masr, has been summoned to appear before Egypt’s Supreme State Security Prosecution (SSSP) today for investigation in a new criminal case against her, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Regional Impact, Yasmine Ahmed, said: “It is utterly disgraceful that the Egyptian authorities are once again targeting Lina Atallah for the brave and professional reporting by her team at Mada Masr. This is the sixth case against Mada Masr and its journalists in six years, illustrating the Egyptian authorities’ relentless harassment of independent journalists who challenge the state-controlled narrative. “Lina Atallah has been bravely leading one of the few remaining independent media outlets in Egypt and should never have been targeted with these successive investigations. Egyptian authorities must immediately end all judicial harassment against her and Mada Masr staff. “This summons is part of a wider crackdown on independent media and freedom of expression. It comes just weeks after the arbitrary arrest of six journalists at the fact-checking platform Matsadaash who are being held in pretrial detention pending criminal investigation. Instead of repeatedly subjecting journalists to unjust prosecution on unfounded terrorism-related or ‘false news’ charges, the authorities must release the Matsadaash journalists and allow journalists to investigate and report free from intimidation, harassment or fear of reprisals.” Background Over the past six years, Lina Atallah and her Mada Masr colleagues have faced six politically motivated prosecutions over their reporting. Most recently, on 4 August 2025, the authorities summoned Atallah for questioning on unfounded charges, including “spreading false news” and “operating a website without a license,” over an article published on 31 July 2025 about deteriorating detention conditions in Badr 3 prison. She was released on bail pending investigation. Criminal investigations against her and Mada Masr staff remain open in five cases. Mada Masr has unsuccessfully sought a license since 2018. On the same day that prosecutors summoned Lina Atallah for investigation, President Abdelfattah al-Sisi spoke at the conference Egypt Forum 2026, saying at the government “listens, discusses, and accepts any criticism.” The ongoing crackdown on journalists has also targeted those who took part in a sit-in at the Journalists Syndicate, which began on 3 October 2026, in solidarity with the arbitrarily detained Matsadaash journalists . On 5 October 2026, journalist Rasha Azab, a participant, was questioned over a social media post criticizing the ministry of interior. The SSSP accused her of terrorism-related charges and released her on bail of EGP 10,000. On 19 October 2026, the journalists announced they were suspending the sit-in. At least 18 journalists were jailed in Egypt a, according to the Committee to Protect Journalists. Hundreds of websites remain blocked in the country, including Mada Masr, other media outlets and independent NGOs.

https://www.azattyq.org/a/qazaqstan-aske.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР Қазақстан әскери қызметтің екі кезеңнен тұратын үлгісіне көшпек 22 қазан 2026 жыл, 06:18 Қазақстан әскери қызметтің екі кезеңнен тұратын үлгісіне көшпек Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Google-да басымдық бер Қауіпсіздік кеңесінің отырысы. Астана, 21 қазан 2026 жыл. 21 қазанда президент Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаев әскери реформа мәселелері бойынша Қауіпсіздік кеңесінің отырысын өткізді. Бұл жөнінде Ақорда хабарлады. Онда әскери реформа жоспарының жобасы талқыланды. Ақорданың хабарлауынша, жоспар қарулы күштердің құрылымы мен құрамын қайта қарау, басқару және қорғанысты жоспарлау тетіктерін жетілдіру, дрон күштерін құру, сондай-ақ армияның негізгі компоненттерін нығайтуды қарастырады. Жоспарды Қауіпсіздік кеңесі төрағасының орынбасары Аида Балаева таныстырды. "Бұл реформаның маңызды аспектісі – мерзімді әскери қызметтің екі кезеңнен тұратын үлгісіне көшу. Әскерге шақырылғандар алғашқы алты айда оқу орталықтарында даярлықтан өтеді. Кейінгі алты айда тікелей әскери бөлімдерде қызмет етеді. Бұл кезеңде жауынгерлік даярлыққа және бөлімшелер құрамында міндеттерді орындауға басымдық беріледі" деп Ақорда жиында айтылғаннан үзінді келтіреді. Ақорданың жазуынша, әскери қызметкерлердің қауіпсіздігін қамтамасыз ету және құқықтарын қорғауға ерекше назар аударылмақ. "Әскери консультанттар мен әскери қызметшілер істері жөніндегі уәкіл институттарын құру жоспарланып отыр. Сондай-ақ жарғыға сай келмейтін іс-әрекетке жол бермеу және әскери тәртіпті күшейту шаралары қабылданады" деп жазылған Ақорда хабарламасында. Жиын кезінде Тоқаев "қысқа мерзімде заманауи, ұтқыр әрі технологиялық тұрғыдан озық армия құрудың" маңызын айтқан. "Қарулы күштердің сапасын өзгерту міндеті қойылды. Өзгерістер басқару ісін, әскери қызметшілерді даярлауды, кадр саясатын, әскери білім беруді, қорғанысты жоспарлау мен технологиялық жарақтандыруды қамтуға тиіс. Әскери қызметтің қауіпсіздігіне, әскерге басшылық ету мәдениетіне және мемлекет ресурстарын тиімді пайдалануға айрықша мән беру керек. Армияның қоғаммен қарым-қатынасы да өзгеруге тиіс. Кешенді реформа қажет. Бұл істе толыққанды шешімдер қабылданбайынша, көздеген нәтижеге жету мүмкін емес" деді Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаев. Мұндай ақпарат Каспийдегі оқу-әскери жаттығу кезінде қаза болған 14 сарбаздың өлімінен кейін бір айға жуық уақыт өткенде айтылып отыр. 24 қыркүйекте Каспийдегі әскери жаттығу кезінде күн бұзылып, қайықтан суға түскен 17 сарбазды қатты толқын ағызып әкеткен. Олардың 14-і қаза тауып , үшеуі аман қалған. Бейбіт заманда жас азаматтардың қазаға ұшырауы қоғамда үлкен резонанс туғызып, әлеуметтік желіде жұрт билік пен әскери басшылықты сынға алды. Осыдан кейін Қазақстан президенті Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаев қорғаныс министрлігі басшылығын түгел ауыстырған . Бұдан бөлек, Тоқаев қорғаныс министрлігіне кешенді тексеру жүргізуді тапсырған . Сарбаздар қазасына себеп болған оқиғаға байланысты қылмыстық іс қозғалып, бес әскери басшы: әскери-теңіз күштері қолбасшысының бірінші орынбасары – штаб бастығы, екі әскери бөлімнің командирі, теңіз жаяу әскері ротасының және "Қайсар" қатерінің командирлері күдікті ретінде ұсталған . Қазақстандықтардың елге келгенін адвокат Мейірман Шекеев 22 қазанда желіде хабарлап , видеосын жариялады. Ақпараттары туыстары растады. “12 адам болу керек. Нақты тізімін анам жасауы керек. Әлі есіміз шығып жүр. Шымкентке кеше (21 қазан) кешкі сағат 6-да келді. Сосын таңертең Астанаға келді” деді шымкенттік Айнабек Келдібектің әпкесі Азаттыққа. Оның сөзінше, Ресейден әлі оралмағандар да бар. Әзірге Ресейден нақты қанша адам оралғаны белгісіз. Қазақстан сыртқы істер министрлігі соңғы мәлімет бойынша ақпарат бермеді. Қазан айының басында Ресейге жұмыс істеуге барған бір топ қазақстандық Қазақстан президенті Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаевтан көмек сұраған. Олар өздерін әскери келісімшартқа қол қоюға мәжбүрлеп, Украинадағы соғысқа жібергенін мәлімдеген. 28 қыркүйекте Азаттық сауалына жауап берген Қазақстан сыртқы істер министрлігі соғысқа әкетілуі мүмкін деген азаматтарды елге қайтаруда жәрдем көрсетуді сұрап, Ресей сыртқы істер министрлігіне нота жолдағанын хабарлаған. 2 қазанда министрлік “соғыс қимылдары жүрiп жатқан аймақта жүрген қазақстандықтардың туыстарынан келетін өтініштерді қабылдау үшін” арнайы желі ашылғанын мәлімдеді. 7 қазанда Қазақстан сыртқы істер министрлігі соғысқа алынған қазақстандықтарды қайтару бойынша Ресеймен келіссөз жүргізіп жатқанын хабарлады. Мекеме өкілдерінің айтуынша, жедел желіге түскен өтініштер бойынша деректер тексерілген. Ресей қарулы күштерінің қатарына қосылған қазақстандықтардың туыстары 7 қазанда Астанадағы сыртқы істер министрлігіне барып, жастарды елге қайтаруға көмектесуді сұрады. Олардың айтуынша, жақындары Ресейге жұмыс істеуге кеткен, кейін отбасына өзін әскери келісімшартқа қол қоюға мәжбүрлегенін айтқан. Кейін туыстарымен бірге министрлікке барған заңгер Мейірман Шекеев ата-аналардың өтініштерін қарау үшін арнайы комиссия құрылғанын хабарлады. Украинада Ресей жағында соғысып жүрген Қазақстан азаматтарының нақты саны ресми түрде анықталмаған. Орталық Азияда жолаушы таситын жүрдек пойыз қатынасын және соған сәйкес инфрақұрылымды дамытып жатқан жалғыз елден көршілерінің үйренері бар ма? "Шапшаң, жайлы әрі таңғаларлықтай оңай" – үндістандық тревел-блогер Barnali Biswas өзбекстандық "Афрасиаб" пойызын осылай сипаттаған . Оның әріптесі, тағы бір блогер Shailab Vlogs 7 Өзбекстанға жасаған сапары жайлы: "Премиум бизнес-классқа жататын орындықтарына, заманауи интерьеріне және қызмет деңгейіне көңіл толады" деп пікір қосқан . Ресейліктер де "Әмір Темірдің ұрпақтары жылдамдық жағынан РЖД-мен Ресейдің теміржол компаниясы бәсекеге түсіп жатыр" деп қызғаныш аралас көңіл-күймен атап өткен . Ал Өзбекстан болса Орталық Азия өңіріндегі теміржол қатынасының көшбасшысы мәртебесін одан ары нығайтып жатыр. Алғашқы "Афрасиаб" және кейін жаңғырған көлік желісі Өзбекстанда кейінгі он бес жылда жолаушы пойыздарын дамыту шын мәнінде серпін алды. "Афрасиаб" брендімен шығатын испаниялық Talgo 250 пойызының алғашқы жолаушы рейсі елді Ислам Каримов басқарып тұрған кезде, яғни 2011 жылы іске қосылған. Ол Ташкент пен Самарқанды байланыстырып, жолға кететін уақыт бұрынғы төрт сағаттан екі сағатқа дейін қысқарқан. Жылдар өте, Шавкат Мирзияев билікке келгесін және туристерге шекара ашылғаннан кейін "Афрасиаб" Өзбекстанның бетке ұстар брендіне айналды: елге шеттен келетін қонақтар легі еселеп көбейіп, мемлекет астанасы мен ортағасырлық көрікті тарихи орындарға бай Самарқанның арасына қатынайтын жүрдек пойызға сұраныс тіптен артты. 2016 жылдың қыркүйегінде "Афрасиаб" бағыты Ұлы Жібек жолында ғасырлар бойы маңызды сауда торабы қызметін атқарған және бірегей сәулет ескерткіштерін сақтап қалған тағы бір көне қала – Бұхараға дейін жетті . Қазір "Афрасиаб" Ташкенттен Самарқан, Бұхара, Қаршы және Науаи қалаларына қатынайды. "Афрасиаб" жүрдек пойызының жолсерігі Өзбекстан билігі мұнымен тоқтап қалмақ емес. Ташкент осы тәжірибені ары қарай кеңейтіп жатыр. Үкімет батыс пен оңтүстікке қарай тарайтын теміржол желісін электрге қосуды бастады . Оңтүстікте Ауғанстанмен шекараға жақын жатқан Термез қаласына (Ташкенттен шамамен 650 шақырым) пойыз қатынасын жолға қою жоспарда бар. Мұндағы мақсат – турист тарту ғана емес, Орталық Азиядағы халқы ең көп елдің түкпір-түкпірін жүрдек пойыз қатынасымен қамтамасыз ету екені анық. Биыл мамыр айында Өзбекстанда ортағасырлық Хорезмшахтар мемлекетінің соңғы билеушісінің құрметіне аталған "Жәлеләддин Мәңгіберді" атты жүйрік жаңа электр пойызы іске қосылды . Оңтүстіккореялық Hyundai Rotem компаниясы жасап шығарған пойыз Ташкент – Самарқан – Бұхара – Хиуа бағыты бойынша қатынайды. Ташкент пен шалғайдағы тарихи орталық – Хиуа арасында (шамамен 1000 шақырым) жол жүруге кететін уақыт екі есеге жуық қысқарып, 14 сағаттан жеті жарым сағатқа түсті. "Жәлеләддин Мәңгіберді" сағатына 250 шақырымға дейін жылдамдықпен жүйтки алады және Өзбекстан климатына бейімделген: +50 °C-қа дейінгі аптап ыстыққа, −40 °C-қа дейінгі аязға төзімді әрі Қызылқұмның шөл дала шаңынан қорғалған деп сипаттайды тасымалдаушы компания. Қыркүйектің ортасында президент Мирзияевтің Оңтүстік Кореяға сапары барысында Ташкент қазір іске асырылып жатқан келісімшарттарға қосымша тағы сегіз жүрдек электр пойызын сатып алу жөнінде Hyundai Rotem компаниясымен шартқа отырды . Олар өзге бағыттарға қоса, Ташкенттен елдің шығысындағы Әндіжанға дейінгі стратегиялық маңызы бар әрі техникалық тұрғыдан күрделі, тау арқылы өтетін бағытқа қатынайтын болады деп жоспарланған. Оңтүстік Корея басылымдарының хабарлауынша , бұл пойыздар Өзбекстан жағдайына бейімделіп жобаланған – олардың негізгі тораптары ыстықтан және құмнан сенімді қорғалған. Пойыздың доңғалақ жұбы кореялық стандарт өлшемнен (1435 мм) өзгеше – 1520 мм рельс табанына шақтап жасалған. Кореялық жаңа пойыз жобада көзделген жылдамдығымен жүйтки алуы үшін Өзбекстанда теміржол рельстері, автоматика жүйелері мен электр желілері жаңғыртылып жатыр деп хабарлады елдің көлік министрлігі. Үкімет ел астанасы мен өзге қалалар арасында ғана рейс ашып қоймай, шалғай облыстарды да өзара байланыстырып жатыр. 2026 жылдың тамыз және қыркүйек айларында Өзбекстанда қытайлық CRRC Dalian компаниясы жасап шығарған, ең жоғарғы жылдамдығы сағатына 160 шақырымға дейін жететін қазіргі заманғы CR200J электр пойыздары іске қосылды – олар Хиуа мен Бұхара арасына қатынайды. 10 қыркүйектен бастап CR200J электр пойызы Ташкенттен Әндіжанға да қатынай бастады . 2027 жылдың наурыз айында Өзбекстан билігі Ташкент пен Қарақалпақстан астанасы Нөкіс арасына қатынайтын жүрдек пойызды іске қосуды жоспарлап отыр. Осы аптада ондаған журналист Құрылтайдың төрағасы Айбек Дәдебайға ұжымдық хат жолдап, брифинг өткізу ережесін өзгертуді талап етті.
